name: Listen to news and broadcasts
summary: Any working radio picks up broadcasts: car radios, clock radios and hand-crank emergency radios. AM and shortwave signals travel hundreds or thousands of kilometres after dark, so scan at night. A long wire strung high pulls in far more stations, and a crystal radio built from wire and a diode needs no power at all.

parts.why: Any receiver: car, clock, crank and shortwave radios
A better antenna brings in more stations
Long wire antennas, and coils for a crystal radio
Detector diode for a crystal radio
Tuning coil for a crystal radio

tips: A car radio works as long as the battery does. Keep an eye on the battery so you can still start the car.
Write down the frequency and time of any station you hear, and check back at the same time.
A crystal radio needs a long antenna and a good earth, like a metal stake or a buried water pipe.
